random forests are a combination classifier, that the generalization error converges a.s., and that the error rate depends on the strength and correlation of the individual trees.

the random forest classifier is a combination of tree classifiers such that each tree is constructed as follows: a) Draw n random vectors, with each vector consisting of m random numbers uniformly distributed over [0, 1]; these vectors are used to split the data in the nodes of the trees; b) If the data is binary, randomly pick one of the two possible terminal nodes for each split.

(1) the strength of a forest of trees is related to the correlation between the trees, (2) the error of a forest is related to the strength of the trees and the correlation between the tree, (3) the correlation between trees can be controlled using a random selection of inputs to split each node, (4) the strength of each tree can be controlled using the number of inputs used to split each node.
